name: Recession-odds-shock regime gate (credit-spread cross-up + macro risk-off) arming a long defensive-equity rotation
rationale: Thesis: rising recession odds = a risk-off regime that front-runs equity drawdowns and a defensive-sector bid. The Kalshi/arXiv 2604.01431 work finds the recession-probability channel (KXRECSSNBER) is the MOST stable macro-risk signal OOS; Polymarket recession + emergency-cut odds spiked with the 2025 tariff shock as risk assets fell, i.e. recession odds LEAD risk-asset drawdowns. The real pm recession-odds series is not yet ingested, so we proxy the recession-risk regime with credit_spread (BOUNDED, +IC in our own scan, ~3yr PIT) which is the market-priced analogue of rising recession probability. The HEDGE-FUND-UNTAKEABLE edge is not credit itself (macro funds trade credit) but the GATING combination on slow, low-glamour daily defensive ETFs that are too low-capacity for macro funds: arm a long defensive-equity rotation only when the recession-risk regime TRANSITIONS on. Entry fires ONLY on credit_spread cross_up through a fitted high quantile (a regime TRANSITION, never a static level) AND while macro_regime is gt a fitted risk-off floor. Long-only. DISCONFIRMER 1 (beta control): an unconditional long-hold of the same defensive ETFs over the same window — defensives drift up anyway; the gated version MUST beat this net of 10bps fees or it is beta not signal. DISCONFIRMER 2 (DRIFTING-trap control): credit_spread as a raw lt/gt LEVEL with no cross/quantile transition MUST NOT survive — if a static level works, the edge was a level-in-disguise, not the recession-regime transition. If the unconditional defensive hold matches the gated PnL, the hypothesis is rejected.
catalyst: Recession-odds shock: credit spreads widen through a trailing high (the market-priced recession-probability proxy) while macro regime turns risk-off — historically front-runs equity weakness and a defensive-sector (staples/utilities) bid.
